title: Scrambled Eggs with Smoked Salmon
subtitle: soft, creamy eggs with ribbons of smoked salmon
excerpt: Perfectly scrambled eggs should be soft, barely set, and slightly glossy. Smoked salmon goes in at the very end so it warms without cooking. This is a quick luxury that works for a weekend breakfast or a light supper.
sourceNotes: Scrambled eggs with smoked salmon became a staple of the British hotel breakfast and later a popular home brunch dish. Smoked salmon has been produced in Britain, especially Scotland, since the early 20th century.

content.text: The secret to soft scrambled eggs is low heat and patience. Stir constantly and take the pan off the heat before they look fully done -- they will keep cooking from the heat of the pan.

items.prepNote: use 150g smoked salmon, torn into pieces
use 2 slices of good bread, toasted

content.text: Beat the eggs with the cream. Season with black pepper only -- the smoked salmon will add salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over very low heat. Pour in the eggs.
Stir slowly and constantly with a spatula, scraping the bottom of the pan. This should take 5 to 7 minutes. Do not rush.
When the eggs are just barely set and still look slightly wet, remove from the heat. Fold in the smoked salmon.
Serve immediately on toast, scattered with chives.

items.cause: Cooked too fast over high heat
items.fix: Use the lowest heat you have and stir continuously.
Fold salmon in only when eggs are off the heat.

content.text: Soft scrambled eggs and smoked salmon became a British weekend institution in the latter half of the 20th century. Smoked salmon, once expensive and reserved for special occasions, became widely available and affordable. This dish sits in the space between effort and elegance -- quick to make, easy to get wrong, and very good when done right.
